newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai rice closes down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai rice closes down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai rice futures ended down on Tuesday on technical profit-taking, traders said.
The key September 1996 contract ended at 2,527 yuan ($304) per tonne, losing six yuan. It opened at 2,533 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 2,536 and a low of 2,515.
October fell nine yuan to 2,506 per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 11,250 tonnes from 7,050.
"Profit-taking by retail investors was responsible for today's falls but institutional support emerged at low levels," one trader said.
Traders expect rice to test the key 2,500-yuan support level in the short term.
They said it would not breach an upper resistance level at 2,540/50 because of weak market sentiment.
